regressions.decompiled: _44 = mem[64] / mem[mem[64]] = 32 / _45 = mem[128] / mem[mem[64] + 32] = mem[128] ... return memory from mem[64] len _44 + 32 * _45 - mem[64] + 64
regressions.old: mem[mem[64]] = 32 / mem[mem[64] + 32] = mem[128] ... return memory from mem[64] len 32 * mem[128] + 64
regressions.issue: The return length was folded to '32 * mem[128] + 64'. It now carries '_44 - mem[64]' with _44 = mem[64] and no store to mem[64] in between, plus two new variables. The return is still raw memory in both texts.
regressions.rule: x = mem[64] with no store to mem[64] in between makes 'x - mem[64]' 0. Better still, decode the return as Array(len=mem[128], ..), as done elsewhere in this build.

improvements: Custom errors decoded with their arguments (0x09639043, cd[..]; 0x96c6fd1e, 0; 0xe450d38c, caller, balanceOf[caller], ..; 0xbc28f241, ext_call.return_data[0]) instead of raw memory. SFC calls named (claimRewards, withdraw, slashingRefundRatio). The withdraw revert is flattened to 'if not _param2: revert ..' before the call. P1 2 -> 0, P6 13 -> 0, P2 4 -> 0.
notes: Diff 630 lines, reviewed function by function. The call/log/store/revert sequences are unchanged apart from names, decoded reverts and the flattened withdraw/revert order. The 4 source loops are unchanged whiles. The pack header lists no P4, but the text still has 20 one-element concat keys (round-1 count) by my regex.
summary: Low regression: two raw returns lost their folded length ('_44 + 32 * _45 - mem[64] + 64'). Custom errors and SFC calls are decoded, and P1/P6 are gone.
